sections.content: How many people stayed in Seaton after gaining qualifications?

Seaton is a small town in the North West. Seaton does not have its own university.

Seaton has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Seaton ended up with:

  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

In Seaton, 255 state school pupils sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 2011 school years.

Of these, 60 (24%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as definied by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 120 (47%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Seaton to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Seaton's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Seaton in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there in 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, all affected students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

In 2018 to 2019, 25% of qualified non-graduates living in Seaton had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 100 qualified non-graduates from our cohort living in Seaton, compared with the 120 qualified non-graduates who sat their GCSEs there.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 75% of qualified non-graduates in Seaton had sat their GCSEs there, while 25% had moved there from elsewhere.
